newsitem.title: BRAZIL: VW to build Audi cars in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: VW to build Audi cars in Brazil.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Brazil unit will start manufacturing by the end of 1998 the Audi-A3 model at a new plant it is building in Brazil, the company said in a statement Wednesday.

Volkswagen said it would invest at least $750 million in the factory in the southern city of Curitiba, capital of Parana state, which will also produce the new Passat model and the popular Golf model.
The plant will generate between 2,500-3,000 jobs and another 8,000 indirect jobs, VW said.

"The new factory ought to be concluded in December 1998, when the first of the A-3s destined for the domestic market and for export to Latin America will be coming off the production line," the company said.
Production of the Golf will begin in mid-1999 and of the Passat at the end of 1999 with final capacity envisaged at 150 Audi A-3s, 150 Passats and 400 Golfs per day.
VW said the new Curitiba plant would be Audi's largest operation outside Germany.

The German car maker, for decades a high-profile fixture on the Brazilian automotive scene, is one of dozens of international vehicle manufacturers to chose to take advantage of a special Brazilian Car Industry Regime.
The regime allows car makers to import vehicles and parts at half the usual tariff if they also export an equal amount.
Several countries, including the United States and the European Union, have demanded World Trade Organization consultations, alleging the regime breaches WTO rules.
But that has not prevented car makers from pledging to invest at least $20 billion in Brazil by the turn of the century.
Brazil and its Mercosur trade block partners Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay are widely regarded as one of the world's most promising car markets, along with China.
